newsitem.title: USA: Alliance files for Chapter 11 reorganization.
newsitem.headline: Alliance files for Chapter 11 reorganization.

text.p: Alliance Entertainment Corp said Monday it filed to reorganize its core businesses under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code.
It is seeking to restructure about $322 million of long-term debt and revolving credit and $204.1 million in trade and similar obligations at May 31.

The company is also in talks to sell its Red Ant unit, its Los Angeles-based new release product label specializing in alternative rock and urban music. The unit, part of its proprietary products group, was excluded from the filing.
The company received a preliminary proposal for consideration with respect to a $50 million equity investment in connection with a reorganization plan.
It has entered a loan agreement with a syndicate of banks led by Chase Manhattan that provides for about $50 million of debtor-in-possession (DIP) financing for the filing entities.
The company requested court approval to use $3 million in cash collateral pending interim approval of the DIP financing, which is expected to be approved by the Court as early as Wednesday.
The company said the $50 million financing will allow the filing entities to continue operations uninterrupted, purchase new goods, and improve operating margins.

Beside Red Ant, Alliance excluded from the Chapter 11 filing Castle Communications, the U.K.-based catalog and re-issue label, and St. Clair Entertainment Group, its Canadian subsidiary. Both businesses are also part of the proprietary products group.
The company said the exclusion of Castle and St. Clair was related to their status as non- domestic entities.

"Alliance's growth through acquisition resulted in the accumulation of burdensome levels of debt and interest expense at a time of little or no growth in the domestic music industry," said Al Teller, chairman, chief executive and president.

Teller said he expects daily operations of the filing entities will continue uninterrupted, and that those businesses will proceed with "substantially" more liquidity than has been available in recent months.
He also said he expects employees of the filing entities will continue to be paid, and customer orders will be filled promptly.
